newsitem.title: INDIA: Flights resume after Delhi airport fire.
newsitem.headline: Flights resume after Delhi airport fire.

text.p: Indian Airlines flights operating from the fire-charred terminal of New Delhi airport have been shifted to an adjacent terminal, airport officials said on Wednesday.
"No flights will be cancelled," Harbans Kumar, the airport director, told Reuters.
An early morning fire destroyed the main departure terminal exclusively used by the state-owned Indian Airlines on Wednesday but no casualties were reported, airport officials and police said.
The blaze erupted at 0330 a.m. (2200 GMT Tuesday) and was still smouldering from debris seven hours later. The terminal was completely gutted.
Flight services were disrupted for three hours but resumed later from an adjacent terminal for private domestic airlines, officials said.
An official in charge of airport operations, Roby Lal, said the fire broke out from the airport's restaurant and kitchen staff raised the alarm. Its cause was not immediately known.
Airport officials said 10 international flights, due to land at an adjacent terminal, were diverted in the morning.
"It will take at least four months to reconstruct the terminal," Kumar said.
The destroyed terminal handled some 20,000 people daily.
